answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake bond before it can trade, like a wharf charging every ship a deposit before docking. A newcomer with no verifiable work history starts with a tiny transaction limit, and the limit grows only as honest trades accumulate, the way basalt hardens under pressure over time. A flood of fake identities then faces a real cost: each clone must lock funds and wait, while a single comet-like burst of new accounts earns nothing, because trust is earned slowly and slashed when fraud is proven.
